name: meta-tagging platform - concept definition component
note: Every score in this product is recomputed in the browser from verdicts.json and cases.json. Nothing is precomputed except the verdicts themselves. An agent given only these files can reproduce every published number; that is the acceptance test for machine accessibility, and it is checked at build time by TOOLS/build_platform_data.py.
license: CC BY 4.0 for the tag layer. Paper text is (c) its authors and is linked, never redistributed here; quotes are short and for identification.

papers.json.what: one record per paper a visitor can put in a corpus

cases.json.what: one record per case; `quote` is an exact substring of the paper

fields.status: 'P' asserted art | 'N' asserted not art | 'U' the literature does not decide

definitions.json.what: the rival definitions, their gate verdict and their published score

verdicts.json.what: definition id -> one character per case, in case index order

how_to_score: Pick a set of paper ids. Take every case whose paper is in the set and whose status is P or N. For a definition, compare its verdict character to the status ('1' vs 'P' = true positive). Then MCC = (TP*TN - FP*FN) / sqrt((TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN)). The 'circular' definition must score near +1.000 on any corpus; if it does not, the coding contradicts itself and no other number in that view may be read.
limitations: Single coder: the cases were coded in one pass, so two-independent-coder reliability is not met and is not claimed.
Scores are comparable only WITHIN one run. Instruction wording alone moves MCC by about 0.12 for an identical definition.
Confidence intervals overlap heavily at the top; ranks are not separable.
The corpus tilts contemporary. That was a deliberate choice and it affects every number here.
